First, define the program.
Then, allocate budgets to entity managers.
Next, distribute employee points.
Employees can visit the store and redeem points for available merchandise.

ShelfMerch receives and processes the orders.

Save this sequence for your next company store planning session.
For an enterprise walkthrough, visit shelfmerch.io.

#EmployeeSwag #CompanyStore #MerchPlanning

A company swag store needs a clear path from budget to employee choice.

In ShelfMerch's enterprise workflow, the company receives a budget, entity managers receive allocations, and employees receive points to redeem for available merch. ShelfMerch receives and processes the resulting orders.

Before launch, agree who owns each step and what employees need to know.

What would your team want to see demonstrated first? Explore a ShelfMerch demo at https://shelfmerch.io.

Before launching an employee swag store, answer four questions:

• Who owns the company program?
• Who manages each entity's budget?
• How will employees receive and redeem points?
• What happens after an order is placed?

ShelfMerch's enterprise workflow covers company and entity budgets, catalog-backed stores, employee points, and order processing.

Bring your organizational structure to a demo: https://shelfmerch.io.

Allocated budget. Employee points. Merchandise orders.

Three connected stages to keep distinct when planning corporate gifting.

Start by defining the program and naming each budget owner. Then agree how entity allocations and employee points will work for your team.

What is the first budget question your finance or HR team would ask?
Discuss your setup in a ShelfMerch demo at shelfmerch.io.

Your starting checklist:

ShelfMerch supports company and entity budgets as part of its enterprise merch workflow.

A practical corporate gifting budget explains who the program serves and who owns each allocation.

For a company store program, distinguish the company budget, entity allocations, employee points, and merchandise orders. Each describes a different stage of the workflow.

ShelfMerch lets enterprise teams work with company and entity budgets, stores, kits, and employee points.

Before assigning a merch budget across teams, write a short program brief.

Include the audience, program purpose, responsible manager, proposed store or kit approach, and questions about points and service terms.

That gives the budget conversation a concrete starting point. In ShelfMerch's enterprise workflow, managers receive allocated budgets and can distribute employee points for store redemption.

Explore the workflow with your team's requirements: https://shelfmerch.io.

A store gives employees a place to choose from available merch.

ShelfMerch supports sending kits and creating stores within its enterprise workflow.

Will your team curate a kit?
Will employees choose through a store?
Who will own the budget and program communication?

Bring those answers to the product discussion, then confirm current catalog options and service details.

With a kit, your team curates the selection. With a store, employees choose from the available merchandise.

Define the recipient group, program owner, budget questions, and whether you want a curated kit or store-based employee choice. Confirm availability and service details before announcing the program.
